candidate.claim: Two-timescale meta-skill evolution improves held-out performance over single-level skill evolution, with component ablations indicating domain-dependent contributions.

primary_source.title: MetaSkill-Evolve: Recursive Self-Improvement of LLM Agents via Two-Timescale Meta-Skill Evolution

evaluation_design.data_split: stratified train/validation/held-out-test partitions; test is not observed by evolution loop
evaluation_design.default_iteration_budget: 5 fast iterations; H=2; two meta-updates under the default

meta_update_horizon.design: three meta-updates held fixed; H=2/4/8 implies 6/12/24 fast iterations, respectively
meta_update_horizon.important_difference: The paper explicitly notes this H=2 sweep point has 6 fast iterations and 3 meta-updates and therefore is not the same operating point as the default main-table full system with 5 fast iterations and 2 meta-updates.

material_scope_and_attribution_correctio.detail: The paper's baseline definition says Single-Level Evolution uses the fast loop with slow loop frozen AND K_max=1 AND no cross-branch sharing AND no meta-skill updates. The main-results prose then says the +6.38/+8.05/+1.92 difference is attributable to meta-skill adaptation because 'the only difference' is whether meta-skill files evolve. These statements are not fully consistent. Appendix Table 3 says the `disable_meta_updates` row exactly reproduces Single-Level but does not clarify in the text whether that flag also enforces the K_max=1/no-cross-branch restrictions. Therefore the numerical Full-vs-Single-Level gap is primary-verified, but causal wording should be 'full two-timescale configuration over the paper's Single-Level baseline' rather than a clean one-factor estimate of meta-skill rewriting alone unless implementation/config provenance resolves the ambiguity.

The accessible v1 text reports no token/dollar cost table and no matched-compute Single-Level control. Full slow-loop execution entails additional pipeline calls, and the Single-Level baseline is described with a smaller child budget/no cross-branch. Do not interpret +6.38/+8.05/+1.92 as gain at matched inference cost.

Section 4.4 says the horizon sweep probes the trade-off 'while holding total compute fixed', but it simultaneously scales fast iterations as 6/12/24 while holding only the number of meta-updates fixed at three. Unless a narrower compute definition is intended, total execution work is not obviously matched. Preserve the reported accuracy sweep, but do not use it as a clean compute-matched causal comparison.

No occurrence of 'seed' was found in the accessible arXiv v1 HTML and the main/ablation tables report point accuracies without run-to-run standard deviations or confidence intervals. Treat the reported differences as exact outcomes of the documented experimental runs, not estimates with demonstrated between-run stability.

The remove-one-component rows establish that each altered configuration scores below Full on these held-out partitions, but each intervention changes operational behavior (e.g. -alpha fixes K=2; -pi feeds raw analysis to Evolver). This supports component sensitivity under the tested implementation, not orthogonal additive causal contributions.

confidence: high for primary table values and held-out protocol; medium for the paper's causal attribution of the Full-vs-Single-Level difference to slow-loop meta-skill adaptation alone because the v1 baseline description is internally ambiguous
resolved_gap: The self-improvement worker's previously secondary +6.38/+8.05/+1.92 Full-vs-Single-Level values are now directly primary-verified, as are component-ablation and horizon-sweep values.
unresolved: Official implementation/config inspection that determines whether `disable_meta_updates` alone preserves Full K_max/cross-branch behavior or whether it is the composite Single-Level configuration described in Section 4.1.
Matched-inference-cost comparison of Full vs fixed-meta fast-loop evolution.
